solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carry out charge by number of animals?

parts.note: charging by how many animals there are is charging per pet, PER meaning for each and PET a domestic animal
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A kennel owner wonders whether to bill by headcount of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a rate per pet is literally a charge by the number of animals. The pieces run in answer order, PER PET before RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime or deed is to commit or carry it out.

clue.text: Grandma, perhaps, drinks litre of liquid

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the letter for litre goes inside the other piece

parts.note: one grandma is your father's mother, i.e. pa's ma

explanation.surface: An old lady downs a litre of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks pa's ma as one example of a grandma (the other is ma's ma).
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale fluid part of blood in which the cells are suspended.

clue.text: Refuse further exams after finals are switched

indicators.note: once the final two letters of the word for repeat exams change places

parts.note: resits are exams taken again after a failure

explanation.surface: A student declines more tests once the final papers are reorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after finals are switched' swaps only the last two letters, TS becoming ST. 'Finals' looks like university exams, adding to the exam-themed disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to refuse to comply with or give in to something.

clue.text: Speak out, and continue after former partner flees, upset

indicators.note: the phrase for continuing comes after the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to press on is to continue

indicators.note: upset shows the letters of the word flees are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone vents and carries on once a jilted ex runs off in a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges FLEES into ESELF, which closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To express yourself is to put your thoughts or feelings into words, to speak your mind.

clue.text: Reports of official mistake likewise curtailed

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a match official
to err is to make a mistake

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: also means likewise

explanation.surface: Complaints about a referee's blunder are, similarly, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' is a verb here, giving ERR; 'curtailed' docks the O of ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Referrals are cases passed on to someone else, such as a doctor or authority, in effect reports sent onward.

clue.text: Member of school of trout swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the fish's letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A trout swimming among a school of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' pretends to be a shoal of fish; it is an educational establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a teacher on the staff of a school or college.

clue.text: Baltic resident of guest-house

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, the letters sitting inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: Someone from the Baltic lodging at a B&B.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in guEST-House, across the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: Esth is an old word for an Estonian, a native of one of the Baltic states.

clue.text: Avoid social workers — they're worn out, going downhill fast

definitions.text: they're worn out, going downhill fast

parts.note: to skip something is to avoid it
ants are social insects and many are workers in the colony

explanation.surface: A tired person dodges social services and hurtles downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social workers' is not a profession but insects; 'worn out' means worn outdoors, not exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers worn outdoors for skiing, the sport of going downhill fast.

clue.text: Excited to draw around beginning of December, a turning point

parts.note: high can mean excited or elated

indicators.note: around puts the tie letters either side of the picked letter

parts.note: to tie is to draw a game

indicators.note: beginning of picks the first letter of December

explanation.surface: Thrilled to sketch the start of December, a pivotal moment.
explanation.definitionFit: High tide is when the sea stops rising and starts to fall, literally where the tide turns.

clue.text: Right, plane — don't bust out of this!

definitions.text: Right, plane — don't bust out of this!

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the opening words are broken out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A controller tells a pilot sternly to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RIGHT PLANE DONT rearrange into the answer, and the whole clue is also an order to a plane circling an airport; 'bust out' suggests a jailbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes stacked over a busy airport fly an oval circuit until given a landing slot.

clue.text: One telling tales gets a question in return

indicators.note: in return means the word for question is read backwards

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it, so pose stands for question

explanation.surface: A snitch is asked something back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling tales' hints at a sneak, but means a storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Plump kind of pigeon working out?

parts.note: plump means fat
a homing pigeon finds its way home

explanation.surface: A tubby bird taking exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like gym exercise but means figuring out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathoming a problem means getting to the bottom of it, understanding it.

clue.text: Manipulator of people on half of continent

parts.note: the mass or masses are the people

indicators.note: half of keeps the first three of the continent's six letters

parts.note: Europe is a continent

explanation.surface: A puppet-master controlling the population of half a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manipulator' suggests a schemer, but here it is someone who kneads muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur manipulates the body's muscles by rubbing and kneading.

clue.text: Amend socialist platform

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a raft is a floating platform

explanation.surface: Change the left-wing party manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'platform' suggests a political programme, but it is a floating one.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft a document is to write a new version of it, amending it.

clue.text: Done in, two beasts of burden eat half of dinner, being shattered

indicators.note: two asks for the donkey word twice

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a beast of burden

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled in another order
half of takes the first three letters of dinner

explanation.surface: Exhausted donkeys wolfing half their supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being shattered' rearranges EAT and DIN into INATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in is slang for killed, and assassinated means murdered for political reasons.

clue.text: Clawed, small crustacean showed sign of injury

parts.note: a crab is a crustacean
bleeding is a sign of injury

explanation.surface: A little crab nipped someone, who bled.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch or grope about with the fingers or claws.

clue.text: Love former queen welcomes in Society Editor that's fixated

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: welcoming someone in takes them inside, so the letter goes within the queen's name

parts.note: Bess was Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: An old queen invites the society columnist in and becomes obsessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Queen Bess was the popular name of Elizabeth I; 'Love' is O because a zero score in tennis is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed is fixated on one thing, unable to think of anything else.

clue.text: Tops Snow White initially with apples?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: eaters are dessert apples, as opposed to cookers; the question mark marks it as one type

explanation.surface: Snow White, the fairy-tale apple victim, wearing tops.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain apples are 'cookers' or 'eaters' (eating apples), which is the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweaters are jumpers, knitted garments worn on the upper body, so tops.

clue.text: Go on the fiddle repeatedly and be ingratiating

definitions.meaning: to draw a bow across a violin and scrape away at it, over and over
to behave obsequiously, bowing low and drawing the foot back

explanation.surface: A cheat keeps up the swindle while fawning on the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests cheating, but it is a violin being played.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes servile deference and also the actions of a fiddler.

clue.text: Rickety plane over India from Kathmandu?

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An unsafe aircraft flying over India out of Kathmandu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts the anagram above I.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali describes someone or something from Nepal, whose capital is Kathmandu.

clue.text: Old hand travels northward to either side of land regularly

indicators.note: the reversed word sits on both sides of the picked letters
in a down clue, northward means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: goes means travels

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of land

explanation.surface: A veteran heads north and skirts the coast at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'northward' means read from the bottom up; 'regularly' picks the even letters of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old, experienced sailor, a seasoned old hand.

clue.text: Electronic errors, perhaps, in passes

parts.note: lapses are slips, errors being an example

explanation.surface: Electronic glitches turn up in mountain passes.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Disreputable soak commandeering daughter's car

indicators.note: commandeering means seizing, so the shuffled letters take the daughter's letter inside
disreputable means not respectable, so the letters are in disarray

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A shady drunk hijacks his daughter's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disreputable' rearranges SOAK into SKOA, with D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech make of car.

clue.text: Attend promotion for bookmaker?

definitions.meaning: to show up or be present
a betting shop's sign inviting punters to place a wager on the premises

explanation.surface: Turn up to a bookie's launch event.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the letters differently, 'Bet here!' as an advertising slogan; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be there is to attend or be present.

clue.text: One scouring earth — see young birds flying round about

indicators.note: flying round about pictures the letters whirling into a new order

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
owlets are young owls

explanation.surface: Fledglings circle a patch of earth being cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is an abrasive pad of fine steel threads used for scouring pans.

clue.text: Country ditching no good runner

indicators.note: ditching means discarding, so those letters are removed

parts.note: England is a country

explanation.surface: A nation drops its useless athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a fleet-footed antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, a fast runner.

clue.text: Blow —-!

definitions.meaning: a mild oath of annoyance, as in 'Blow it!'
the printed punctuation mark itself, a long horizontal stroke

explanation.definitionFit: Dash is a mild exclamation like 'Blow!', and the printed stroke is a dash.

clue.text: Old man's moves, inappropriately candid and gauche at first

indicators.note: inappropriately means in an unsuitable way, so the letters are put in the wrong order
at first takes the opening letter of gauche

explanation.surface: An awkward, frank remark about how Grandad dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriately' rearranges CANDID AND into DADDANCIN, then G ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad dancing is the embarrassing, uncoordinated dancing of a middle-aged father at a party.
